lines.japanese: 朝から妙に気持ちが上ずってしまったので、どうにも落ちつかない。
lines.english: I'd been strangely keyed up since morning and couldn't settle.

lines.japanese: 学校に来てはみたものの、誰かこの高鳴りをぶつける相手はいないかと思って探してみた。
lines.english: Though I'd come to school, I found myself hunting for someone to unload this pounding excitement on.

lines.japanese: と言ってもタカシが学校では大人しくしてたからな、知り合いなんてそんなにいるわけじゃないんだけど……。
lines.english: Takashi had kept his head down at school, though, so naturally he didn't have many acquaintances...

lines.japanese: 誰かいないか、からかい甲斐がありそうな愉快で面白いやつ。
lines.english: Wasn't there anyone around? Someone fun. Someone amusing. Someone worth teasing.

lines.japanese: うおっ。
lines.english: Whoa.

lines.japanese: あ、危ない、目が合うところだった。そういえば玉泉もこの学校だったな。からかい甲斐のあると言えば適任なんだが、話しかけるのはマズイな。
lines.english: C-close. Our eyes had almost met. Right, Tamaizumi went to this school too. She was prime teasing material, but approaching her would be asking for trouble.

lines.japanese: 誰か友人らしい女の子と話してる。というか、女の子がなにか話しかけてるのに一人ずんずん進んでいってる。
lines.english: She was with a girl who looked like a friend. Or rather, the girl kept talking to her while Tamaizumi marched steadily on by herself.

lines.japanese: あいつ学校ではどんなカンジなのだろう。あまり近づくと危険だけど、ちょっと盗み聞きしてみよう。
lines.english: What was she like at school, anyway? Getting too close would be dangerous, but a little eavesdropping couldn't hurt.

lines.japanese: 俺はロッカーの影に隠れて玉泉を見守った。
lines.english: I hid behind the lockers and watched Tamaizumi.

lines.japanese: 「朝からそんなんじゃ、いつかオブローモフになるよ」
lines.english: “Keep starting your mornings like that and you'll turn into Oblomov someday.”

lines.japanese: オブローモフってなんだ……。
lines.english: What the hell was Oblomov...?

lines.japanese: なんだかロシアっぽい名前だけど、意味がさっぱり分からない。
lines.english: The name sounded vaguely Russian, but I had no idea what it meant.

lines.japanese: 追いかけてことの内容を確かめたかったが、残念ながら声をかけることは出来ないので俺は消化不良のままその姿を見送った。
lines.english: I wanted to follow them and find out what they were talking about. Unfortunately, I couldn't exactly call out to her, so I watched them go with my curiosity painfully unsatisfied.

lines.japanese: なんだか余計に胸にもやもやを抱えたままになったな……誰か他のやつ通らないかな。
lines.english: Great. Now the feeling in my chest was even murkier... Wasn't anybody else going to come by?

lines.japanese: わあ。
lines.english: Oh, my.

lines.japanese: 要注意人物が肩を並べて登校してきた。関わりたくないことこの上ない。
lines.english: Two high-risk subjects arrived at school shoulder to shoulder. I wanted nothing whatsoever to do with them.

lines.japanese: だがやつらが二人揃うとどんな会話になるんだ。そうだ、普段俺のことを観察してる連中を俺が観察してやろう。
lines.english: But what did those two talk about when they were alone together? Yes. The people who usually observed me were about to be observed in turn.

lines.japanese: 俺はロッカーの影に隠れて要注意人物たちを見守った。
lines.english: I hid behind the lockers and watched the high-risk subjects.

lines.japanese: 「そういえば最近、蛎崎どうなの？」
lines.english: “Come to think of it, how's Kakizaki doing lately?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、来年放送の『自分戦隊オレンジャー』に『コシフリーヌ女王』役で出演決定だってさ」
lines.english: “Oh, she landed the part of Queen Hip-Shaker in next year's *Self Squadron Me-Ranger*.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ、やるねえ。『無免ライダー・チャリ』の前にやるんだっけ？」
lines.english: “Wow, good for her. That airs before *Unlicensed Rider: Bicycle*, right?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ？　おまえ特撮とか知ってんだ。『巨乳刑事ボイン』とか面白いぞ」
lines.english: “Huh? You know live-action hero shows? *Busty Detective Boing* is pretty good.”

lines.japanese: 「見ないって。私、女の子だよ。弟がいたから『キメドラマン・シャブ』まで見てたけどね。じょわっち」
lines.english: “I don’t watch that stuff. I’m a girl. My little brother got me watching through *Ultrameth: Speed*, but that was it. Jowatch!”

lines.japanese: 「あれはその次の『アガってきたキメドラマン』の方が面白ぇぞ。技術が格段に上がってるからなァ」
lines.english: “The next one, *Ultrameth Rising*, is better. The production values jumped way up.”

lines.japanese: 「だーから見てないってば。『キメドラマン・アイス』までだよ。キメドラの母とかキメドラ三兄弟が出てきたあたり」
lines.english: “I keep telling you, I didn't watch it. I stopped at *Ultrameth: Ice*—around when Mother of Ultrameth and the Three Ultrameth Brothers showed up.”

lines.japanese: 言ってることがまったく分からない……。
lines.english: I didn't understand a word they were saying...

lines.japanese: なんだったんだろう。ま、まあやつらは、俺の知り合いの中でも奇人と変人に分類される人種だからな。ほうっておこう。
lines.english: What the hell had that been? W-well, even among my acquaintances, those two belonged to the species classified as oddballs and freaks. Best leave them alone.

lines.japanese: くそ、余計にやるせなさが増したじゃないか。このまま教室に行こうものならどんよりとした一日を送ることになってしまう。もう少し知能レベルの低そうな会話するやつを見つけて遊んでもらおう。
lines.english: Damn it. Now I felt even more desolate. If I went straight to class like this, a gray and joyless day awaited me. I needed to find somebody capable of a stupider conversation and make them entertain me.

lines.japanese: ずおおっ。
lines.english: Whoa.

lines.japanese: また愉快な組み合わせだ。個々はそれほど興味を惹かれる素材じゃないけど、どんな化学反応を起こすか見てみたいという好奇心が働く。
lines.english: Another delightful combination. Neither specimen interested me much on its own, but curiosity demanded that I see what sort of chemical reaction they produced together.

lines.japanese: 山科は明らかに迷惑そうだが、残念だが俺も混ざりたくないので助け舟は出せん。許せ山科、そしてフォーエバー。
lines.english: Yamashina was plainly miserable, but regrettably I had no desire to join them either, so no rescue would be forthcoming. Forgive me, Yamashina. And farewell forever.

lines.japanese: 俺はロッカーの影に隠れて化学反応を見守った。
lines.english: I hid behind the lockers and observed the chemical reaction.

lines.japanese: 「なー、山科ー」
lines.english: “Heeey, Yamashina.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yes?”

lines.japanese: 「やっぱおまえみたいなセージュン系の下着って白とか決まってんの」
lines.english: “So, does a pure-and-innocent type like you have to wear white underwear or what?”

lines.japanese: 「記号的に区別されるのはそう見られる方も楽でいいけど、ときとして狂気をかきたてられるのは、ただの身勝手に過ぎないのかもしれない」
lines.english: “Being sorted into symbols may make life easier for the person being watched. But the madness those symbols sometimes arouse may be nothing more than selfishness.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、なに？　つか余計なのいいからイエスかノーで答えろよ」
lines.english: “Huh? Whatever. Skip the extra stuff and answer yes or no.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そーなん？　へえ、じゃあどんな色が好きなん。いま何色よ？」
lines.english: “Oh, really? What colors do you like, then? What color've you got on now?”

lines.japanese: 「冬はつとめてのち巡りあいドドメ色」
lines.english: “In winter, the early morning; thereafter, fateful meetings; mulberry-bruised purple.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　つーかもっと分かりやすい色分けで答えろよ、黒とか紫とか」
lines.english: “Huh? Just give me a normal color I can understand. Black, purple, whatever.”

lines.japanese: 「……ブルーのタータンチェック」
lines.english: “...Blue tartan.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなん着けてんの。かー、私にゃ似合わねーな」
lines.english: “You wear stuff like that? Damn. Wouldn't suit me.”

lines.japanese: 「０の掛け算の答えは全て同じだよ」
lines.english: “Anything multiplied by zero comes out the same.”

lines.japanese: なんなんだこいつら……。
lines.english: What the hell was wrong with these people...?

lines.japanese: ダメだ、会話の知的レベルは低いが、いかんせん低俗にもほどがある。俺はこの学校に絶望して昇降口から離れることにした。
lines.english: No. The intellectual level might have been low, but so was the conversation, in every possible sense. I despaired of this school and abandoned the entrance hall.

lines.japanese: だが一つだけ救いがある。
lines.english: There was, however, one consolation.

lines.japanese: 山科の今日の下着はブルーのタータンチェックなんだあ、いやっほうい。
lines.english: Yamashina was wearing blue tartan underwear today. Yee-haw!

lines.japanese: 俺はスキップしながら階段を上がり教室まで辿りついた。
lines.english: I skipped up the stairs all the way to the classroom.

lines.japanese: 今日も我が班員たちは全員集合した。
lines.english: Once again, every member of my team had assembled.

lines.japanese: 無愛想なカラスはいつも通りとして、プリンセスとブルーのタータンチェックは時折会話をしながら作業を進めてる。うん、いい空気だ。
lines.english: The surly Crow was his usual self, while Princess and Blue Tartan worked on, exchanging the occasional word. Yes. What a pleasant atmosphere.

lines.japanese: 俺が輪に入ってないことを除けばな。
lines.english: Except for the part where I wasn't in it.

lines.japanese: 「山科ー、コレ一年のときに沼いったときだよね」
lines.english: “Yamashina, look. This is from when we went to the marsh in our first year, right?”

lines.japanese: 「くすっ、ホントだ、サフランイエローだね」
lines.english: “Hee hee. It is. Saffron yellow.”

lines.japanese: ていうかこの間から写真を見て無駄話してるだけで仕事してないよこの二人。だが厳しく注意してやる気をなくされるのも困る。
lines.english: Come to think of it, those two had done nothing for some time but look at photographs and chatter. They weren't working at all. But a stern reprimand might kill their motivation.

lines.japanese: さりげない会話からやる気を促そうと思ったが、無難な学園生活を送ってきた俺には話に入る手段がない。俺は手に持っていたコンソメポテチをばきりと握りしめもったいないからきちんと食べた。
lines.english: I tried to spur them on by casually joining the conversation, but my uneventful school life gave me no opening. I crushed the consommé-flavored chips in my fist with a crack, then carefully ate every crumb. Waste not.

lines.japanese: くそ、こうなったら次は無理やりでもいいから話に入ってやる。
lines.english: Damn it. Next time I was forcing my way into the conversation whether they liked it or not.

lines.japanese: 「あ、見てコレ二年のときの文化祭だよね。このときの準備はたるかったなー」
lines.english: “Oh, look! This is from the school festival in our second year. God, the preparation was such a drag.”

lines.japanese: 「ああでも山科なんて楽しそうな顔してるじゃないか、ははは」
lines.english: “But look how happy Yamashina is. Ha ha ha.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、この頃は束の間の夢に身を浸していたからね。毎日が楽しかったよ」
lines.english: “Yes. I was steeped in a fleeting dream then. Every day was happy.”

lines.japanese: 「え、なに？　なんの……」
lines.english: “What? What kind of—”

lines.japanese: 「おいぱね田。どうしてくれるのこの空気」
lines.english: “Hey, Paneda. Look what you did to the mood.”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ、俺！？」
lines.english: “What, me!?”

lines.japanese: 山科が傍から見ても分かるくらい痛々しい笑顔を浮かべてる。え、俺のせいなの？　なんで？
lines.english: Yamashina wore a smile so painful that even an onlooker could see it. Wait, was this my fault? Why?

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そういえばこのすぐ後だったかな。屠殺場の豚は何も知らずに死んでいけるから、幸せなんじゃないかってことに気づいたのは」
lines.english: “Oh, come to think of it, that was shortly before I realized the pigs at a slaughterhouse might be happy. They get to die without ever knowing a thing.”

lines.japanese: 「あの時立ち直れたのはもしかして私にとって不幸だったのかもしれない。だってそれから何度も痛悔の日々を送ることになったんだから」
lines.english: “Perhaps recovering then was my real misfortune. It only meant enduring bitter remorse again and again.”

lines.japanese: 渡来が山科に見えない位置から恨めしそうに俺を睨んできた。くっ、なんてめんどくさい女だ……！
lines.english: From where Yamashina couldn't see her, Watarai shot me a reproachful glare. Ngh. What an exhausting woman...!

lines.japanese: 「た、立ち直ったってことはなにかいいことあったんだよね？　教えてほしいなあ」
lines.english: “Y-you recovered because something good happened, right? I'd love to hear about it.”

lines.japanese: 話題を変えようにも山科のテンションが上がらない限り救いが見えない。俺は何故か頼みこむような口調でお伺いをたてた。
lines.english: Changing the subject would save nothing unless Yamashina's spirits came up with it. For some reason, my question emerged as a plea.

lines.japanese: 「別に聞いても面白くもなんともないよ。あるバンドの曲と詞に救われたの」
lines.english: “It's not an interesting story. A certain band's songs and lyrics saved me.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ、なんてバンド？」
lines.english: “Oh? Which band?”

lines.japanese: 「もう解散してるし、聞いても分からないと思うよ。ロックバードなんて聞いたことないでしょ？」
lines.english: “They've already broken up, and I doubt the name would mean anything to you. You've never heard of Rockbird, have you?”

lines.japanese: 「ロックバード」
lines.english: “Rockbird.”

lines.japanese: 横で黙々と作業を続ける男に目がいった。でもその男は微動だにせず、写真をハサミで切って紙面のスペースとの兼ね合いを試していた。
lines.english: My eyes went to the man working silently beside us. He didn't so much as twitch. He kept trimming photographs with his scissors and testing them against the space on the page.

lines.japanese: 「へえ、山科ロックバード好きなんだ」
lines.english: “So you're a Rockbird fan, Yamashina.”

lines.japanese: 「え、知ってるの？」
lines.english: “What, you know them?”
“Mm. More or less...”

lines.japanese: ていうかそこにいる。だけどバンド名義で出している楽曲は一曲たりとも知らない。
lines.english: One of them was sitting right there. But I didn't know a single song they had released under the band's name.

lines.japanese: 「山科はああいうハードロックが好きなのか」
lines.english: “So you like that kind of hard rock?”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、音楽のジャンルとしては好きじゃないよ。ただ、彼らのリリックやパフォーマンス、そういった部分が私の感性に合ってただけ」
lines.english: “No. I don't like it as a genre. Their lyrics and their performances simply struck something in me.”

lines.japanese: 話題の焦点を広げようかと思ったのに失敗した。参ったな、俺が知ってるロックバードの知識なんてもうないぞ。
lines.english: So much for broadening the subject. Damn it. I had already exhausted everything I knew about Rockbird.

lines.japanese: 「パンク時代じゃなくて今のロクバが好きなんだよね？」
lines.english: “You like the later Rockbird, though, right? Not their punk period.”

lines.japanese: おお助かった。話が良い方向に進むと思ったのか、渡来が助け舟を出してくれた。ていうか後は任せた。
lines.english: Oh, what a relief. Watarai must've thought the conversation was finally headed somewhere good and thrown me a line. Anyway, the rest was hers.

lines.japanese: 「うーん、パンク時代の詞が好きってひともいるけど、私から見ると、んー……」
lines.english: “Hmm. Some people prefer the lyrics from their punk period, but to me they just...”

lines.japanese: 「見ると？」
lines.english: “They seem?”

lines.japanese: 「意味もなく下品なこと言ってるようにしか聞こえなくて」
lines.english: “They sounded like vulgarity for vulgarity's sake.”

lines.japanese: 「クッ」
lines.english: “Kh.”

lines.japanese: 全く会話に入ってこようとしなかった男が、急に笑い声を上げた。他の二人も気になったみたいで視線が年上の男に集まる。
lines.english: The man who had shown no intention of joining us suddenly let out a laugh. The other two noticed, and all eyes turned toward the older man.

lines.japanese: 「ああ悪い。でもおまえいいこと言うよ。案外その通りかもしれないなァ」
lines.english: “Yeah, sorry. But you’ve got a point. You might actually be right.”

lines.japanese: ハリュー・クロードは作業を一時中断すると、ペットボトルのキャップを外して、ミネラルウォーターを喉に流しこんだ。
lines.english: Haryu Claude paused his work, unscrewed the cap of his bottle, and poured mineral water down his throat.

lines.japanese: 「え、えっ？　ロックバード知ってる？」
lines.english: “W-wait. You know Rockbird?”

lines.japanese: 「ああまァ……あんたがファンだっていうなら、その程度には知ってるかなァ」
lines.english: “Well... if you're that much of a fan, I suppose I know them at least that well.”

lines.japanese: 「ぷっ」
lines.english: “Pfft.”

lines.japanese: 吹きだすな、馬鹿。二人同時に笑ったら山科に突っこまれそうだったので、漏れそうになった息をなんとか堪えた。
lines.english: Don't laugh, idiot. If both of us cracked up at once, Yamashina might start asking questions, so I somehow smothered the laugh trying to escape.

lines.japanese: 「うんうん、私も知ってるよ。山科に教えてもらったからねえ」
lines.english: “Mm-hm, I know them too. Yamashina introduced me.”

lines.japanese: 「わっ、すごい。みんな知ってるなんて嬉しいなあ。今までライブハウスとか掲示板で知りあったひととしか話したことなかったんだ」
lines.english: “Wow. That's amazing. I'm so happy all of you know them. Until now, I'd only had people I met at music clubs or on online message boards to talk to about them.”

lines.japanese: おっ、山科の顔に笑顔が戻った。だが明らかに一番知識の薄い俺は、へらへらと曖昧に笑うことしかできなかった。
lines.english: Oh, Yamashina's smile was back. But as the person here with by far the least knowledge, all I could do was grin vaguely.

lines.japanese: 「へえ、ライブまで行ってたの」
lines.english: “Huh. You even went to their shows?”

lines.japanese: 褐色の腕がペットボトルを掴んで、山科のコップに紅茶を注いだ。注がれた側が小さく頭を下げる。礼のつもりなんだろうか。
lines.english: Claude's brown hand picked up a bottle and poured tea into Yamashina's cup. She dipped her head, presumably in thanks.

lines.japanese: 「出したＣＤはパンク時代のも含めて全部持ってるけど、やっぱり生の音だとぜんぜん違うし……それにパフォーマンスとかビジュアルもその瞬間にしか見られないものもあるからね」
lines.english: “I own every CD they released, including the punk-era records. But live, the sound was completely different... And some of the performances and visual touches existed only for that one moment.”

lines.japanese: 「ビジュアル？」
lines.english: “Visuals?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、毎回ステージ衣装も凝ってるし、顔とかも、ね」
lines.english: “Yes. They put so much into the stage costumes every time. And their faces were... you know.”

lines.japanese: 「はははははは」
lines.english: “Ha ha ha ha ha!”

lines.japanese: 「こら、笑うなぱね田。山科に失礼だよね」
lines.english: “Hey, don't laugh, Paneda. That's rude to Yamashina.”

lines.japanese: そう言いつつ、渡来の目には俺よりよっぽどいやらしい色が浮かんでいた。
lines.english: As she said it, Watarai's eyes held a far dirtier gleam than mine.

lines.japanese: 「あ、もし良かったらＣＤ貸すよ？」
lines.english: “Oh, I could lend you the CDs, if you'd like.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、俺も全部持ってるからなァ」
lines.english: “Nah. I own all of them too.”

lines.japanese: 「ホントに？　残念だな、解散する前ならライブにも誘いたかったよ」
lines.english: “Really? What a shame. If they were still together, I would've liked to invite you to a show.”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃムリだな」
lines.english: “That'd be impossible.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ムリだね」
lines.english: “Yeah. Impossible.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、なんで？」
lines.english: “What? Why?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ、俺そういうトコ行く服とか持ってないから」
lines.english: “Oh, uh, I don't own anything I could wear to a place like that.”

lines.japanese: 「うんうん、私も夜遅く帰ると怒られちゃうから」
lines.english: “Right, right. And I'd get in trouble if I came home late.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえ一人暮らしだろ」
lines.english: “You live alone.”

lines.japanese: 「うるさい、余計なこと言うとこっちもバラすぞ」
lines.english: “Shut up. Keep saying stuff you don't need to and I'll spill your secrets too.”

lines.japanese: 「どっちにしろ、解散する前の段階だったら行く価値ねェよ。御影クリヤのＣＤでも買ってりゃいい」
lines.english: “Either way, if we're talking before the breakup, they weren't worth seeing. Buy a Kuriya Mikage CD instead.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、そんなことないよ。ＫｕＲｉＹａは今もカッコいいけど、私はロックバードの頃が好きだったな」
lines.english: “That's not true. KuRiYa is still cool now, but I liked him better in the Rockbird days.”

lines.japanese: 「渡来さんは？　ＣＤ貸そうか？」
lines.english: “What about you, Watarai? Want to borrow a CD?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あはー、だから私は……ま、まあ知ってるけど好みのジャンルではない、かな」
lines.english: “Oh, ha ha... Like I said, I know them, but they're not really my kind of music.”

lines.japanese: 「私も最初から好きだったわけじゃないよ。でも、ある日体に染みこんでくるの。届かない想いや過ぎていく時間、そういったものが」
lines.english: “I didn't love them from the start either. Then one day it seeps into your body—the feelings that never reach anyone, the time slipping past, all of it.”

lines.japanese: 「それを生の音で聞いたときに想いを込められるかどうかで全然違ってくるし、後期はリリシストをバンド名義にしてるものが多かったけど、メンバー全員がそれぞれ深く考えてないとあの音は出せな……あっ」
lines.english: “And when you hear it live, everything depends on whether they can pour those feelings into the sound. In their later work, the lyricist was often credited simply as the band, but unless every member had thought deeply about the words, they could never have made that sound... Oh.”

lines.japanese: 珍しく熱弁をふるった山科は、そこでぽかんとしてる俺たちに気づいたみたいだ。
lines.english: Yamashina had launched into an unusually passionate speech. Apparently she had only now noticed the rest of us staring blankly.

lines.japanese: 「ご、ごめんね、一人ではしゃいじゃって。恥ずかしいね」
lines.english: “S-sorry. I got carried away all by myself. How embarrassing.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ別に……」
lines.english: “Oh, it's fine...”

lines.japanese: 「ふふッ」
lines.english: “Heh.”

lines.japanese: 横目でチラと見たらハリュー・クロードの口端がわずかだけど釣りあがっていた。
lines.english: I stole a sidelong glance at Haryu Claude. One corner of his mouth had risen, ever so slightly.

lines.japanese: 「いいと思うぞ」
lines.english: “I think it's good.”

lines.japanese: 本人も喜んでるみたいだし。こいつは捻くれてるからよく分からないけどな。
lines.english: The man himself seemed pleased, after all. Though with someone that contrary, who could tell?

lines.japanese: 「うん、好きなものがあるってのはいいことだと思うよ。うらやましい」
lines.english: “Yeah. I think having something you love that much is a good thing. I'm jealous.”

lines.japanese: 「それだけ好きなら、きっとロックバードのメンバーも喜んでるよ。ねえ、先輩？」
lines.english: “If you love them that much, I'm sure the members of Rockbird would be happy too. Right, Claude?”

lines.japanese: 「ハッ、どうだかな。なにからなにまで誉めりゃいいってもんでもないだろ」
lines.english: “Hah. Who knows? Doesn't mean you've got to praise every last thing they did.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、確かにドラムのひとだけは微妙だと思う」
lines.english: “Hmm. True. I was never quite sold on their drummer, though.”

lines.japanese: 瞬間、俺と渡来の爆笑の声が教室中に響いた。その前で途端に口を結ぶハリュー・クロード。
lines.english: In the next instant, Watarai and I filled the classroom with howls of laughter. Before us, Haryu Claude's mouth snapped shut.

lines.japanese: 一人事情が分からない山科だけがきょとんとしていた。
lines.english: Only Yamashina, alone in her ignorance, stared at us in puzzlement.

lines.japanese: 渡来とハリュー・クロードが二人で盛りあがっていたので、山科と一緒の帰り道になった。
lines.english: Watarai and Haryu Claude had gotten wrapped up in a conversation, so I ended up walking home with Yamashina.

lines.japanese: ていうか偶然一緒になったんじゃなくて、俺が山科に声をかけた。
lines.english: Or rather, we hadn't simply happened to leave together. I had called out to her.

lines.japanese: 何故なら山科がいなくては俺の作戦が成りたたないからだ。
lines.english: Without Yamashina, my plan wouldn't work.

lines.japanese: 「はあ、今日はテンション上げすぎたなあ私……明日が心配だよ」
lines.english: “Sigh. I got much too excited today... I'm worried about tomorrow.”

lines.japanese: 「明日？　テンション上げすぎて血管でも切れたのか」
lines.english: “Tomorrow? Did all that excitement burst a blood vessel or something?”

lines.japanese: 「治りが分かりやすいから血管の方が楽だけどね」
lines.english: “Blood vessels would be easier. At least you can tell when they've healed.”

lines.japanese: 「はは、面白いこと言うな」
lines.english: “Ha ha. That's a funny thing to say.”

lines.japanese: 面白いこと……だよな？
lines.english: It had been funny... right?

lines.japanese: 「と、ところで実は山科に頼みがあるんだ」
lines.english: “A-anyway, there's something I need to ask you, Yamashina.”

lines.japanese: 「頼み？　私に？」
lines.english: “A favor? From me?”

lines.japanese: 俺は話題を変えるのも兼ねて本題に移ることにした。
lines.english: I took the opportunity to change the subject and moved on to the real business.

lines.japanese: 「入院している俺の友達と話したいんだけど、間をとりもって欲しいんだ」
lines.english: “There’s a friend of mine in the hospital I need to talk to. Could you help me get him on the line?”

lines.japanese: 「私に？」
lines.english: “Me?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、実はその友人は看護婦マニアで、看護婦からの電話じゃないとすぐに切ってしまうんだ。だから看護婦のふりをして俺に繋いで欲しい」
lines.english: “Yeah. See, this friend of mine is a nurse fanatic, and if the call isn't from a nurse, he hangs up immediately. So I need you to pretend you're one and then pass the phone to me.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、別にいいよ」
lines.english: “Sure. I don’t mind.”

lines.japanese: 「素晴らしい！　さすがは山科、里芋を箸でつかめる女はやることが違うな。マーベラス！」
lines.english: “Marvelous! That's Yamashina for you. A woman who can pick up taro with chopsticks simply operates on another level. Marvelous!”

lines.japanese: 俺は番号を呼びだして通話ボタンを押すと、それを山科に渡した。
lines.english: I brought up the number, pressed Call, and handed her the phone.

lines.japanese: ぷっ　ぷっ　ぷっ　ぷっ
lines.english: Beep. Beep. Beep. Beep.

lines.japanese: ぷるるるるっ……
lines.english: Rrrring...

lines.japanese: 「はいもしもし、またかけてきたの？」
lines.english: “Hello? You're calling again?”

lines.japanese: 「もしもし」
lines.english: “Hello?”

lines.japanese: 「へっ、女の子？」
lines.english: “Huh? A girl?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あれ？　これってイタ電じゃ……えと、キミ誰？」
lines.english: “W-wait, I thought this was a prank call... Um, who is this?”

lines.japanese: 「ナースだけど」
lines.english: “I'm a nurse.”

lines.japanese: 「ああそうなんだあ……ええっナース！　ナースってなに！」
lines.english: “Oh, I see... Wait, a nurse!? What do you mean, a nurse?”

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　ナース嫌い？」
lines.english: “What? Don't you like nurses?”

lines.japanese: 「まあナースっていうか、女の子だったらそりゃ歓迎だけどぉ、だけど、なんでいきなし俺の電話に？」
lines.english: “Well, nurse or not, I'm obviously happy to hear from a girl, but why'd you suddenly call my phone?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、隣にいる子が話したいって言うから。代わるね」
lines.english: “Yeah. The guy next to me wants to talk to you. I’ll put him on.”

lines.japanese: 「え、ええ？　もっかすっと、この病院の看護師さんが俺の番号調べて？　おいおいどの看護師さんだよ。内科の木下さんかな、それとも整形外科の白川さん？」
lines.english: “W-wait. You mean a nurse at this hospital looked up my number? Hey, which one are you? Kinoshita from internal medicine? Or Shirakawa in orthopedics?”

lines.japanese: 「もしもし！？　森里君！　俺だよ、羽田だよ！」
lines.english: “Hello!? Morisato! It's me, Haneda!”

lines.japanese: 「おまえかよ！」
lines.english: “You bastard!”

lines.japanese: 「森里君、どうして前回切っちゃったんだよ。ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Morisato, why'd you hang up on me last time? I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「うるせーハゲ！　イタ電かけて来んじゃねーよ、死ねハゲ！」
lines.english: “Shut up, baldy! Quit prank-calling me! Drop dead, baldy!”

lines.japanese: 「ひ、酷いよ、俺は森里君の体が心配なだけなのに！　調子はどうなの森里君」
lines.english: “Th-that's horrible! I only called because I'm worried about you! How are you feeling, Morisato?”

lines.japanese: 「あ～？　まあ順調に回復してっから、来週には退院できるらしいけど」
lines.english: “Huh? Recovery's going fine. They say I'll be out next week.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ、よかったね森里君。じゃあ退院祝いに髪を切るハサミを持っていくよ」
lines.english: “That's great, Morisato. I'll bring you a pair of haircutting scissors as a discharge present.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、イラネーから。髪切る予定とか今ンとこねーし」
lines.english: “No thanks. I'm not planning on cutting my hair anytime soon.”

lines.japanese: 「そんな！　切った方がいいよ、だってそのロンゲうざいもん。うざいっていうか存在自体いらないんじゃないかな。もう剃っちゃいなよ。ね、すぱっと一発すっきりしちゃいなよ」
lines.english: “What? You should! That long hair is obnoxious. Actually, the world might be better off without it. Why not shave it all off? Come on—one clean pass and you’ll feel so much better.”

lines.japanese: プツッ
lines.english: Click.

lines.japanese: あ、切られた。
lines.english: Oh. He cut me off.

lines.japanese: なるほど、電話を切ることで髪を切ることを意思表示したわけだね。さすが森里君、次に会うときはバリカンを持っていってあげないと。
lines.english: I see. By cutting the call, he had declared his intention to cut his hair. Brilliant, Morisato. I would have to bring clippers next time I saw him.

lines.japanese: それに少し話も出来たし一歩前進だ。次はもっと長く話せるといいな。
lines.english: Besides, we'd managed to talk a little. That was progress. Perhaps next time we could talk longer.
